title: Batch 2: lightning, deepest ocean, no sleep

lines.say: You just got struck by lightning.
Quick, guess how hot that bolt was.
Five times hotter than the surface of the Sun.
Up to a billion volts, in a single flash.
Some of it races over your skin, instead of through you.
It can leave a pattern like a fern on your skin.
And here's the surprise: about nine out of ten people survive.
One park ranger was struck seven times, and lived through every one.
The worst place to be is out in the open, or under a tree. A car with a metal roof is safer.
How close has lightning ever come to you?
You're sinking to the deepest point on Earth.
The first people to go down took a submarine. Guess how long the trip took. Answer at the end.
It's eleven kilometres down. Mount Everest would fit, with two kilometres to spare.
By two hundred metres, it's twilight. By a thousand, there's no sunlight at all.
The only light comes from animals that glow.
The water is just above freezing.
And the pressure is over a thousand times stronger. Like an elephant standing on your thumb.
In 1960, two men rode a submarine down here. On the way, a window cracked.
It took them almost five hours to reach the bottom.
Would you make that trip? Yes or no?
You decide to stop sleeping.
In 1964, a seventeen-year-old really did it. Guess how many days he lasted.
Day two: he couldn't say simple tongue-twisters, or tell what things were just by touch.
Day three: he felt sick every single morning.
Day five: he started seeing things that weren't there.
He was forgetting things, and snapping at people.
He lasted eleven days. Two hundred and sixty-four hours. A world record.
Then he slept for fourteen hours straight.
Guinness stopped accepting this record. It's too dangerous.
What's the longest you've ever stayed awake?
